newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition jet pilot defects to Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition jet pilot defects to Taleban.

text.p: An Afghan opposition pilot defected with his jet fighter to the Taleban Islamic government on Tuesday and landed in the eastern city of Jalalabad, the official Kabul radio said.
The broadcast, monitored in Islamabad, said pilot Naqibullah had defected after he had been ordered by his commanders to bomb public utilities in the Taleban-held Kabul province.

"Naqibullah's patriotism and sense of Islamic duties prevented him from carrying out such operations and he handed over his plane to the Islamic State of Afghanistan," the Taleban-controlled radio said.
Earlier, a Pakistan-based private Afghan news service had described Naqibullah as a general, and said he had defected with his Russian-made Su-22 jet.
The Afghan Islamic Press said the pilot declared loyalty to the purist Islamic Taleban militia after arriving in Jalalabad from the northern opposition stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif.

The defection follows a series of bombing raids launched by northern opposition leader General Abdul Malik on Kabul and the western city of Herat in the past few days. Taleban planes attacked the opposition-held city of Maimana last week.
The radio also said that an isolated force of Taleban militia beat back an opposition attack in the northeastern town of Kunduz on Tuesday and captured the nearby Yarganak district.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
